findings.text: Local datetime, date and time values are stored with a fixed-offset zone (LocalDatetime, LocalDate or LocalTime), and their wall-clock fields are the original local values. `v.In(time.UTC)` shifts the wall clock by that offset before formatting. In a UTC+2 zone, `1979-05-27T07:32:00` is encoded as `1979-05-27T05:32:00`, so encoding corrupts the value and does not round-trip. Format `v` directly instead.

`localOffset` is taken once from `time.Now().Zone()`, so every local datetime gets the offset in force today. Under DST, a winter date parsed in summer, or the reverse, carries the wrong offset. Also, `time.Time` values from a real `time.Local` zone are not recognised as local by the encoder.

1.reason: parse.go:377-380 builds LocalDatetime/LocalDate/LocalTime as time.FixedZone values using the offset from time.Now() at package init, whereas the old code used ParseInLocation(time.Local), so a local datetime from the other side of a DST change now gets the wrong offset and therefore the wrong instant; this is separate from the reference bug, where the encoder's v.In(time.UTC) shifts the written value.
